{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-nm-x","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"98ec430c8a0e5abef544c73fc1db9b73a5356d729dd3cf9a1747d6f5ab8a4f2a","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-nm-class-std:lineage:45","source_registry_sha256":"22599efcb4852b796972acef6eb09f4cfe8d16ca15887f7ea7660c7748b4df92","source_liveness_sha256":"6766993f61347d495f390e08c7d8b1c44de597b6249cdb10686ea7f9f38e1ea3"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Lighting and communicating with other road users","heading":"C — Lighting and communicating with other road users","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Lighting and communicating with other road users

FACT_ID: sec09-F01 | anchor: A01
Use high beams when no vehicle is oncoming, while observing the separate low-beam guidance for following and heavy traffic. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec09-F02 | anchor: A01
The handbook says high beams provide twice the viewing distance of low beams. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec09-F03 | anchor: A01
High-beam visibility is especially useful on unfamiliar roads, in work zones and where people may be beside the road. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec09-F04 | anchor: A01
Dim high beams when an approaching vehicle is about one block away. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec09-F05 | anchor: A01
When following within 200 feet, or driving in heavy traffic, switch to low beams. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec09-F06 | anchor: A01
Choose low beams in fog, heavy snowfall or heavy rain because high-beam reflections create glare. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec09-F07 | anchor: A01
Use the vehicle’s fog lights too, if it has them, in the described fog, heavy snow or heavy rain. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec09-F08 | anchor: A01
Parking lamps alone are unsuitable for driving; they serve parked vehicles. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec09-F09 | anchor: A01
Turn on headlights when other road users are difficult to see, helping them see your vehicle too. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec09-F10 | anchor: A01
When you use windshield wipers, also switch on the headlights. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec09-F11 | anchor: A01
Switch on headlights as daylight starts fading so other drivers can see you. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec09-F12 | anchor: A01
Use headlights while traveling away from sunrise or sunset because drivers facing you may struggle to see you. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec09-F13 | anchor: A01
A brief headlight flick, when needed, can alert another road user to your presence. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec09-F14 | anchor: A01
Use the horn when doing so can prevent a collision; without immediate danger, use a light tap. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec09-F15 | anchor: A01
A light horn tap can alert a pedestrian or cyclist who appears headed into your travel lane. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec09-F16 | anchor: A01
When overtaking a driver who begins moving into your lane, a light horn tap can warn that driver. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec09-F17 | anchor: A01
A light horn tap can help when a driver is inattentive or may not see your vehicle. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec09-F18 | anchor: A01
The handbook suggests a light horn tap near a blind hill, sharp bend or narrow-alley exit where you cannot see ahead. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec09-F19 | anchor: A02
In danger, use a sharp horn blast if a child or older person is about to enter the street. [A01] [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec09-F20 | anchor: A02
In danger, use a sharp horn blast when another vehicle may hit you. [A01] [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec09-F21 | anchor: A02
In danger, use a sharp horn blast if your uncontrolled vehicle is heading toward someone. [A01] [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec09-F22 | anchor: A02
Use a turn signal before a lane change, either turn, a merge or parking. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec09-F23 | anchor: A02
Signal each change of direction even when no other road user is visible. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec09-F24 | anchor: A02
Begin the turn signal no less than 100 feet before turning. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec09-F25 | anchor: A02
If a vehicle may enter between you and the intended turn, wait until you pass it before signaling to avoid implying an earlier turn. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec09-F26 | anchor: A02
After turning or changing lanes, check that the signal has canceled and switch it off yourself if necessary. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec09-F27 | anchor: A03
Brake lamps tell following drivers that your vehicle is slowing. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec09-F28 | anchor: A03
Begin slowing as early as safety permits; if time allows, warn the following driver before a sudden slowdown or stop. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0023]

Misconceptions: parking lamps do not replace driving headlights; signal cancellation needs checking.
Mnemonics: see, be seen, signal, then check cancellation.
Glossary: glare is reflected light that impairs seeing; emergency flashers identify vehicle trouble.
Dynamic facts: local controls, vehicle lighting equipment and current lighting law require checking.
